newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ABN-AMRO H.G. rates Zalakeramia a 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: ABN-AMRO H.G. rates Zalakeramia a 'buy'.

text.p: Shares in Hungarian tile manufacturer Zalakeramia are undervalued and do not reflect the company's outlook, ABN-AMRO Hoare Govett said in an analyst report, rating the stock a 'buy'.

"Currently trading at a discount to its tile-making peers, Zalakeramia's share price does not reflect the very positive medium- and long-term outlook for the stock," Tommy Erdei, ABN- AMRO Hoare Govett's Budapest-based analyst said.
Zalakeramia shares are trading at a discount to comparable stocks when measured by enterprise value/earnings (EV/E), he said.
"This measure -- rather than the more conventional price/earnings ratio -- takes account of Zalakeramia's net cash in comparison with the rest of the industry, which has net debt," Erdei said.
Comparable companies in the Czech Republic and in the developed economies trade at EV/E levels of between 10 and 20 times on 1997 net income, he said.
"We believe that the shares should be trading approximately 26 to 39 percent higher," Erdei said. "This is based on the financial forecast and our expectations of the acquisition."
Zalakeramia recently announced acquisitions plans and will hold an extraordinary shareholders meeting on February 12 to discuss issues related to its planned new acquisitions.
"We strongly believe that these acquisitions will add value within two years," Erdei said.

Zalakeramia announced in January that after having examined some 20 companies in the previous 18 months it believed that three companies were of serious interest. To fund these acquisitions the board is seeking shareholders' approval for the issue of between 0.9 million and 1.2 million new ordinary shares.

"The company's investment projects are expected to make a return on invested capital of 100 percent within three years and management has already demonstrated its ability to realise its investment objectives.
